title: An edit
description: An edit: the video cut from the takes, for each device type it names. Anything in a clip, or at the top, can be given again under a device type, and applies only to that type's video.

$schema.description: The URL of the schema the file is written against, for editors. Optional; a file is read against this Retake's schema whatever it names.

intent.description: What the video is there to show. Not read by the render.

devices.description: The device types it makes a video for.

takeAudioVolume.description: The level of the take's own sound, where a clip plays it.

background.description: The colour of letterbox bands, and of the corners a turn uncovers.

turns.description: How the video shows the device turning. letterboxed: the app stays upright, landscape letterboxed on the canvas. device: the video stays in the device's frame.

touchColor.description: The colour touches are drawn in: a filled ring, its fill at 45% of the colour's opacity and its rim at 90%.

iphone.description: Overrides for iphone's video, laid over the rest key by key.

clip.description: A stretch of a take, played in order.

id.description: Names the clip, for a caption to run on into it. Unique in the edit.

intent.description: What the clip is there to show, for whoever changes the video later. Not read by the render.

take.description: The scene whose latest successful take the clip is cut from.

from.description: Where the clip starts in the take.

speed.description: How fast it plays: 2 is twice as fast.

crossfade.description: Seconds it cross-fades in over the clip before.

audioCrossfade.description: Seconds its sound fades in over, when longer than crossfade.

touches.description: Draws the take's touches, from the step log.

touchColor.description: The colour of the clip's touches; the edit's touchColor when not given.

touchColors.description: Colours for single touches, over the clip's or the edit's.

step.description: A step's id, its number from 1, a negative number counting back from the last (-1 is the last), or start or end, the take's own first and last frames.

takeAudio.description: Plays the take's own sound with the clip.

sounds.description: Sound effects, played at normal speed however fast the clip plays.

blurs.description: Blurs over a stretch of the take, for anything private it shows.

stills.description: Frames of other takes, popped in over the clip.

turns.description: How this clip shows the device turning; the edit's turns when not given.

anchor.description: A moment in a take: a step and where to go from it, or plain seconds from the take's start.

oneOf.description: Seconds from the take's start, which the first `retake cut` turns into a step anchor.

step-anchor.description: A step, and where to go from it.

step.description: A step's id, its number from 1, a negative number counting back from the last (-1 is the last), or start or end, the take's own first and last frames.

offset.description: Seconds to move: forward from the step's end, or back from its start.

fraction.description: A share of the gap to the neighbouring step to move: forward from the step's end toward the next step's start, or back from its start toward the previous step's end.

edge.description: Counts the offset or fraction from the step's other edge.

element.description: An element on screen, as VoiceOver knows it: by any of its label, value, identifier, hint and traits.

value.description: Its value: a text field's placeholder, or what's typed in it.

identifier.description: The accessibilityIdentifier the app gives it.

hint.description: Its accessibility hint: what VoiceOver says it does.

traits.description: Traits it has, every one, by The Button Heist's names, as `retake compose` prints them.

occurrence.description: Which of several matching elements, counted from 1 in the order VoiceOver reads the screen.
